java.say: `new DraughtsGame()` makes a game of draughts. Its field `board` is still empty. The variable has the type Game, the general kind.

start() comes from Game, the parent class, and it needs a board. Game does not know which board fits this game. So it calls createBoard(), a method that each subclass fills in. This is the factory method.

java.at: protected Board createBoard() { return new DraughtsBoard(); }
java.say: The real object is a DraughtsGame, so its createBoard() runs. It makes a new DraughtsBoard and returns it: it hands the board back to start().
Back in start(). The new board goes into the field `board`. Game knows it only as a Board, the interface.
Game asks the board to set itself up. It still does not know what kind of board it is.
The DraughtsBoard code runs and sets out its pieces.
start() is done. Game never wrote `new DraughtsBoard()`: that one choice lives in the subclass. A ChessGame makes a ChessBoard in the same place.
